title: ATS Sampling Frame V1
description: The selection of context bundles for a governed annotation round, with the mechanism that selected each one. Balancing is on sampling mechanism and candidate source, never on a presumed conformance outcome: a frame balanced by expected label would decide the question the annotation exists to answer. A constraint that cannot be met is reported unmet rather than quietly relaxed (spec Sections 17.5, 17.7).

seed.description: Selection is deterministic given the corpus and this seed, so a frame can be rebuilt and disputed.

double_annotation_target.description: How many of the selected bundles receive two independent judgments.

authority.description: Which repositories were authorised for annotation, and under what declaration. A bundle drawn from an unauthorised repository is a governance failure, not a sampling choice.

items.description: One authorised repository, with the provenance of the declaration that authorised it. The permission alone is not enough: an operator overlay and a repository's own declaration can authorise identically, and a frame that recorded only the permission would read as though the repository owner had declared in place. `repository_owned` is derived from where the declaration was found, never from the basis it claims.

repository_owned.description: True only for a declaration read from the repository's own .ats/corpus.json. An overlay is false here even when its basis is `owner_declared`, because the basis is a claim and the location is an observation.

review_after.description: When the declaration must be revisited. An overlay that never expires is permanent governance nobody re-consented to, so the frame records the date it comes due.

required_uses.description: The uses every selected bundle had to have been authorised for.

stratum.description: The mechanism that produced the candidate. `low_signal_random_control` is not filler: without it there is no way to estimate how enriched mining is relative to ordinary prose.

shortfall_reason.description: Required whenever selected is below target. A stratum that could not be filled says why rather than appearing complete.

candidate_source.description: What surfaced this span. Recorded so agreement can be read per mechanism rather than pooled.

candidate_rule_ids.description: Rules a detector flagged as possibly applicable. A candidate is not a finding and not a label.

split_group.description: The leakage-closure component this bundle belongs to, so a frame cannot place two members of one component on opposite sides of a later split.

constraints.description: Every distribution constraint, met or not. An unmet constraint is a finding about the corpus and stays visible.

unsatisfiable.description: True when the corpus cannot satisfy the constraint at any sample size, as opposed to this draw having missed it.

expectation_withdrawn.description: Present only on a row demoted from a requirement to an observation. Records the expectation this row no longer asserts, who withdrew it, and why, so a satisfied observation cannot be mistaken for a requirement that was met. A row carrying this key MUST NOT carry 'unsatisfiable': there is no longer a constraint for the corpus to be unable to satisfy.

blinding.description: What is withheld from annotators. A miner prediction is not a gold label, and showing it would anchor the judgment it is supposed to be tested against.
